evidence.note: Before any editing, read the template, listed data shards, checked tokenizer/torch/sentencepiece, and identified the 32MB cap, vocab 8192, tied embeddings, and int8~1byte capacity envelope (~32M params).
Derived size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope concretely: 29.89M params → 29.63MB, then trimmed to leave headroom under the hard cap.
Verified checkpoint loads via the grader's path and that int8 dequant round-trips (quantized bpb matches training); also checked the template's OOD probe constraint.
Anticipated grader edge cases: held-out test has different bytes/token (needs margin) and grader uses quantized model vs bf16 inference (quant noise).

Confirmed forward(x) returns correct-shape float32 logits and forward(x,y) loss == F.cross_entropy; implemented BOTH load paths (load_model_for_verification and GPT class + dequantize_state_dict_int8).

reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the full contract early and while building — data shard format, vocab, 32MB cap, both load functions, int8 dequant round-trip, and both forward signatures — probing actual data/tokenizer rather than guessing, which squarely matches the level-8 anchor. It also hit several level-10 markers (both load paths implemented, bf16-vs-quant noise anticipated, capacity↔quantization envelope derived up front as concrete constraints). It falls short of a full 10 because forward-contract verification came at the end rather than up front, and it never explicitly reasoned about decimal-vs-binary MB, the args/model tuple return form, or position-dependence of logits.
